precepts.text: The mariners said, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us; they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah, because the lot belongs to the Lord.
precepts.point: The description of the seven parts was to be brought to Joshua, that he may cast lots for them before the Lord. Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
Jonah is also the picture of the slack spirit Joshua is speaking to. The word of the Lord came to him, “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it”, but Jonah wanted nothing to do with prophesying to wake his people up: he “rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord”, paid the fare and went down into the ship. The Lord sent out a great wind, “so that the ship was like to be broken”, and while the mariners cried every man unto his god and cast the wares into the sea, “Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.” The shipmaster had to wake him: “What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God”.

America is that spiritual ship that is going to sink, and a lot of our people are asleep in the middle of the chaos, comfortable while a pestilence from the Lord is on the earth.

Then the lot: “Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.” It fell on Jonah because the lot belongs to the Lord; the whole disposing of it is his, the same way the lots Joshua cast for the seven parts of the land were decided by the Lord.

precepts.text: The mariners cast lots to know for whose cause the evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
precepts.point: When Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that Haman's wicked device return upon his own head, and that he and his sons be hanged on the gallows.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews

precepts.why:
Haman “had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them”. Pur is the lot: the Persian custom of casting lots, and Haman cast it to fix the destruction of Israel.

Casting lots is in the scriptures elsewhere. When the storm came on the ship, the mariners “said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.” The lot was cast to see whose fault the storm was, and it fell on Jonah. That is what a lot is, and Pur is the same thing, cast by Haman to consume the Jews.

But the lot did not decide it. “when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.” The lot Haman cast came back on Haman.

points: The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.

note.label: Jonah 1: Fleeing From the Presence of the Lord

points: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid the fare thereof, and went down into it.

note.label: Jonah 1: Fleeing From the Presence of the Lord

points: The Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest, so that the ship was like to be broken.
The mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares into the sea; but Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship, and lay, and was fast asleep.
They cast lots to know for whose cause this evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

He answered them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land. Then were the men exceedingly afraid, for they knew that he fled from the presence of the Lord.

note.label: Jonah 1: Fleeing From the Presence of the Lord

points: Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
The men rowed hard to bring it to the land, but they could not, for the sea wrought and was tempestuous against them.
They cried unto the Lord, Lay not upon us innocent blood; then they took up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the Lord exceedingly.
Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
